title: Elivagar: Efficient Quantum Circuit Search for Classification
problem: Designing performant and noise-robust quantum machine learning circuits is challenging due to exponentially scaling design space and lack of design principles. Existing Quantum Circuit Search methods directly adopt classical Neural Architecture Search approaches that are misaligned with quantum hardware constraints, resulting in high search overheads.
motivation: Efficient and noise-robust quantum machine learning circuits are essential for practical quantum computing applications.
method: Elivagar searches for quantum circuits that are good at classification tasks by using a framework specifically designed for quantum hardware. Instead of copying circuit design methods from classical computers, it accounts for quantum-specific limitations like noise (errors in quantum operations) upfront in the search process. This steers the search away from designs that look good in theory but won't work in real quantum hardware, reducing the search space from exponentially large to manageable.
key_novelty: It accounts for quantum hardware constraints directly in the search process, rather than adapting methods from classical computers.
contributions: Identifies fundamental misalignment between classical NAS and quantum hardware constraints
Proposes Elivagar framework for efficient quantum circuit search tailored to quantum systems
Achieves reduced search overhead compared to existing QCS methods
Enables design of performant and noise-robust quantum circuits
